newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH 1998 BUDGET TALKS START NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH 1998 BUDGET TALKS START NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Talks on the 1998 budget will begin on Monday, July 21 when finance ministers Sauli Niinisto and Arja Alho start a two-day preparation with top officials on the budget proposal, the finance ministry said on Monday.
The finance ministry will hold talks with other ministries from July 23 to July 31, and the government's work on the proposal will begin on August 13, it said.
Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto will hold a news conference after talks on Tuesday, July 22, it added.

The government outlined in February that budget expenditure in 1998 and 1999 would be 191 billion markka and 192 billion markka respectively, down from some 196.5 billion this year, and said on June 2 that proposals would be made according to that decision.
Finland has adopted an austere fiscal policy to curb a rise in state debt, and has said it aims to meet the criteria for joining Economic and Monetary Union among the first in 1999.
